description: An original, jurisdiction-neutral plumbing vendor access, work coordination, and accountable sign-out record for a potable, nonpotable, sanitary, storm, or equipment piping system whose flow, pressure, valves, drainage, leakage, water quality, and damage impacts require traceable control. It connects facility identity, asset-specific evidence, hazards, qualified decisions, exceptions, service status, and accountable closeout without replacing employer procedures or trade judgment.

blocks.label: Record reference and timing
Facility, location, and responsible parties

blocks.guidance: This Plumbing record organizes facts and evidence. It does not replace employer energy-control procedures, permits, manufacturer instructions, required inspection, emergency response, or qualified trade judgment. Stop and route any unsafe or uncertain condition.
blocks.label: Safety and authority boundary

sections.guidance: Open one traceable record, identify the responsible parties, and set the review route.

blocks.label: Plumbing asset and system profile

blocks.guidance: Check only directly observed or source-supported items; explain inaccessible, not applicable, or conflicting evidence below.
items: System, fixture, equipment, pipe, valve, meter, and served-area identities reconcile
Leak, drip, spray, pooling, staining, corrosion, condensation, and moisture paths are recorded
Flow, pressure, temperature, meter, fixture, and drainage observations identify conditions
Shutoff, isolation, check valve, backflow, mixing, balancing, and control status are documented
Traps, vents, drains, cleanouts, strainers, interceptors, and discharge paths are observed
Pipe supports, insulation, sleeves, penetrations, labels, and freeze protection are recorded
Water damage to ceilings, walls, floors, finishes, contents, and electrical equipment is mapped
Sewage, odor, contamination, cross-connection, scald, and water-quality concerns are escalated
Potable-water, water-management, flushing, sampling, and disinfection records are linked when applicable
Hidden, underground, in-wall, above-ceiling, and inaccessible conditions are explicitly limited
Utility, tenant, occupant, infection-control, remediation, and restoration impacts are identified
Recent repairs, recurring leaks, meter trends, and unresolved moisture evidence are linked

items: Vendor identity, employer, contact, work order, and authorized scope reconcile
Required license, credential, training, insurance, and site orientation are confirmed
Work area, route, escort, keys, badges, doors, alarms, and restricted spaces are defined
Host and vendor exchange energy-control procedures and affected-system status
Permits, hot work, confined space, roof, lift, electrical, chemical, or shutdown controls are routed
Tools, materials, parts, chemicals, cylinders, devices, and waste entering the site are traceable
Scope change, unsafe condition, damage, alarm, spill, or service interruption triggers stop and host contact
Sign-out reconciles people, access items, locks, tags, tools, materials, waste, work status, and handoff

blocks.guidance: A checked condition requires immediate protective action, a named owner, qualified review, and a final disposition.
items: Uncontrolled water, sewage, flooding, severe leak, or loss of required service is present
Suspected contamination, cross-connection, backflow, waterborne-pathogen, or potable-water concern exists
Water contacts energized equipment, structural materials, occupied critical space, or sensitive contents
Scalding temperature, pressure hazard, chemical exposure, confined space, or unsafe access is unresolved
Unknown pipe material, insulation, coating, soil, or building material may require specialist review
Required shutdown, isolation, utility coordination, water-management control, or permit is unavailable
Temporary containment, bypass, hose, valve position, or service restoration could create another hazard
Field condition conflicts with drawings, valve maps, meter data, water-quality records, or prior repair evidence

blocks.guidance: Do not resolve a checked stop condition by inference, an unchecked box, or a generic sign-off. Preserve the condition, protective action, authority, evidence, owner, due point, and verified disposition.

sections.guidance: Stop when authority, access, energy control, safety, evidence, or service status is unresolved.

blocks.label: Vendor Sign-In decision, timing, and authority

blocks.guidance: Check only controls supported by referenced evidence; unresolved controls remain open conditions.
items: Facility host confirms vendor identity, authorization, scope, area, and schedule
Qualified owners approve energy, electrical, fire, roof, confined-space, and shutdown controls
Scope changes are approved before new work, equipment, material, or area access
Access credentials, keys, locks, tags, permits, and temporary devices retain clear custody
Work status and any incomplete or unsafe condition are accepted at sign-out
Vendor and facility contacts receive the same restriction, owner, and next action
Qualified plumbing reviewer approves repair method, materials, valves, pressure, and service restoration
Potable-water, cross-connection, temperature, flushing, disinfection, and sampling needs are routed
Water, sewage, moisture, microbial, structural, electrical, and contents impacts have owners
Temporary containment or bypass has a limit, inspection frequency, and removal trigger
Pressure, flow, leak, drainage, temperature, and meter evidence supports the disposition
Occupants, utilities, restoration teams, and water-management owners receive the final status

items: Leak, flow, pressure, drainage, valve, fixture, and meter status is documented after work
